headline: Medium risk: shared-file and output-trust pathways exist, but B lacks write/network surfaces and the pair is docs-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can handle file uploads and broad network egress, so if its outputs are copied into spring-integration-samples workflows, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. B has no documented ingestion surface, so the bridge is inferred rather than direct; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads contain untrusted text and are forwarded into B's processing path, injection is plausible.
IF an operator manually copies Plane output into a Spring Integration flow, prompt-like content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Restrict Plane uploads to trusted sources only.
Add a manual review step before any Plane output enters B.
Strip instructions from uploaded text before reuse.
Use a fixed schema for any handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps and has broad egress, but B shows no data classes touched and no egress. With no shared workspace or authenticated channel documented, leakage is possible mainly through unusual operator bridging, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is manually moved from Plane into B, that data can be exposed in transit.
IF B is configured to ingest Plane exports, any included task or file content may leak.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive files between the agents.
Redact task notes before export from Plane.
Keep B isolated from any shared workspace.
Review outbound destinations used by Plane.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage separation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write the filesystem and B has no documented write, network, or mutable-resource scope. Without overlapping write authority or a shared lockable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk changes.
IF a shared mutable OAuth or git resource is introduced, reassess for write contention.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared assets.
Avoid mounting a common writable directory.
Do not grant overlapping OAuth scopes.
Use separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add resource locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can produce issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, and hyperlinks that a downstream system may treat as authoritative. B is a Spring Integration sample set, so if its flows consume Plane output without validation, errors can cascade into automated processing. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF B consumes Plane-generated records without validation, incorrect tasks or links can propagate.
IF an operator wires Plane exports into a Spring Integration flow, downstream automation may act on bad data.
mitigations: Validate Plane output against a schema before use.
Insert a human approval step for any automated action.
Reject malformed hyperlinks and file references.
Log and diff imported records before processing.
requires-engineering: add provenance and checksum checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane touches files and notes and offers broad egress, while B documents no data classes or residency controls. There is no direct evidence of a residency or retention mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to undocumented handling gaps rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane and then exported into B, retention and residency policies must be checked.
IF B is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter handling rules, the mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Plane exports.
Confirm retention settings before sharing artifacts.
Keep jurisdiction-sensitive data out of the pair.
Document where each agent stores outputs.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
